title: Node.js Quiz
description: Fourteen questions covering the whole Node.js tutorial: the runtime, npm, modules, files, events and streams, HTTP and Express 5, configuration, async code, node:sqlite, testing and deployment.

questions.question: Which of these globals is NOT available in a Node.js script?
questions.explanation: Node has no DOM, so document does not exist. process is Node-specific, while fetch and setTimeout are available in both Node and browsers.

questions.question: `npm install express` records a version range in package.json and the exact resolved version in package-lock.json.
questions.explanation: package.json gets a range such as ^5.1.0; the lockfile pins the precise versions of express and every package it depends on, so later installs reproduce the same tree.

questions.question: Adding `"type": "___"` to package.json makes every .js file in the project an ES module.
questions.explanation: With "type": "module", .js files use import and export; without it they are CommonJS. .mjs and .cjs files ignore the field.

questions.question: The file `hi.txt` contains exactly the two characters `hi`. What is printed?
questions.explanation: Without an encoding argument readFile resolves with a Buffer of raw bytes. A Buffer is an object (typeof gives 'object') and its length is the byte count, 2.

questions.question: Which EventEmitter method registers a listener that runs only the first time the event is emitted?
questions.explanation: once adds a listener that removes itself after its first call; on keeps the listener until off removes it; emit triggers the listeners.

questions.question: In `createServer((req, res) => { ... })` from node:http, which statement is true?
questions.explanation: The request is a readable stream (the body arrives in chunks) and the response is a writable stream that must be finished with res.end. Nothing parses the body for you in node:http.
options: `req` is a readable stream and `res` is a writable stream
`req.body` already contains the parsed JSON body
`res` is sent automatically when the handler returns

questions.question: In Express, `res.___({ ok: true })` serialises the object and sends it with `Content-Type: application/json`.
questions.explanation: res.json always sends JSON, including for strings and numbers; res.send would also send an object as JSON but treats strings as HTML.

questions.question: Requesting an unknown id makes the server log `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`. What is wrong?
questions.explanation: After the 404 response the function keeps running and calls res.json(book) with undefined, attempting a second response. A return in front of the 404 (or an else branch) fixes it.
options: Line 3 is missing `return`, so `res.json(book)` on line 4 runs as well
`Number()` cannot be applied to route parameters
The handler must call `next()` after responding

questions.question: A `DELETE /api/books/3` request succeeds and the API sends no body. Which status code fits best?
questions.explanation: 204 No Content signals success with an intentionally empty body. 201 is for creation, 404 means the resource was not found and 500 is a server failure.

questions.question: When a program is started with `PORT=3000 node app.js`, `process.env.PORT` is the number 3000.
questions.explanation: Environment variables are always strings; process.env.PORT is '3000'. Convert with Number() before doing arithmetic or comparisons with numbers.

questions.question: What is the output order?
questions.explanation: Synchronous code prints sync first. Promise callbacks (microtasks) run as soon as the script finishes, before any timer, so promise comes second and the zero-delay timer last.

questions.question: Why should SQL that includes user input use `?` placeholders instead of string concatenation?
questions.explanation: With placeholders the SQL text and the values travel separately, so a value can never change the statement's structure. That is what prevents SQL injection; it also lets SQLite reuse the compiled statement.
options: Placeholders make the query return rows as arrays
The values are bound separately from the SQL, so input cannot change the statement (no SQL injection)
SQLite rejects string literals in WHERE clauses
Placeholders are required for SELECT statements to return results

questions.question: Run every test file in the project with the built-in runner: `node --___`.
questions.explanation: node --test discovers files such as *.test.js and files under test folders, runs them and prints a report; add --watch to rerun on changes.

questions.question: Which command installs exactly the locked versions of the production dependencies on a server?
questions.explanation: npm ci installs from package-lock.json and fails if it is out of sync; --omit=dev skips devDependencies such as linters and test tools.
